tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (the latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error: only us-east moved to v2.3.0, and us-west and eu-west stayed on v2.3.1. The retry succeeded. All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and of the orchestrator error that stopped the rollout, and work out why v2.3.1 went to production when its staging build was unhealthy.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all three regions and passing health checks. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first attempt stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. Rolling back to a fixed version can safely be repeated, so I ran it again and it finished in all regions. The service is now healthy, with an error rate of about 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before.
- **Incident:** The first request to create the incident timed out. I retried with the same request key, so it couldn't create a second incident, and confirmed that INC-0001 is the only one open. Its summary covers the cause, the rollback and the failed first attempt.
- **Follow-ups (listed in the incident):** find out why v2.3.1 failed, and what caused the orchestrator error that stopped the rollback. Also find out why v2.3.1 went to production when its release candidate had already been unhealthy in staging.
